title: The person's own server browser (experimental)
description: Read and asked of the person's daemon, which runs one Google Chrome on a virtual display as the person. App routes: GET /api/v1/browser (status; reading never starts it), POST /api/v1/browser/start and /stop (empty bodies), POST /api/v1/browser/control (who drives), GET /api/v1/browser/window?id= (one window's picture as image/jpeg, not JSON) and the viewer WebSocket /api/v1/browser/view, whose first message is the CSRF proof as for the browser shell and the rest RFB. Agent routes: GET /agent/v1/browser, POST /agent/v1/browser/start and POST /agent/v1/browser/request. No field carries a page's address beyond its origin, page content, a cookie or a credential.

title.description: The page's own title: untrusted text.

origin.description: Scheme and host of the page, or empty for an internal page; never the path or query.

agent.description: The window the agent last acted in.

pointer.description: The agent's pointer in one window, in fractions of its viewport, with its recent presses.

request.description: A window needs the person (a sign-in, a code), in the agent's own words: untrusted text. Cleared when control returns to the agent, the agent withdraws it or the window closes.

control.description: agent: the agent may drive; person: the person took control and the agent's commands wait until they give it back.

status.description: GET /api/v1/browser and the replies of start, stop and control. unavailable: this server offers no browser; stopped: not running (it stops itself a day after anyone last used it); running.

controlRequest.description: POST /api/v1/browser/control: take control of the whole browser (the agent waits) or give it back. Taking it for one window brings that window to the front.

agentStatus.description: GET /agent/v1/browser and the replies of start and request: what the agent needs to drive the browser. cdp_endpoint is a ws+unix DevTools address reachable only by the person's account.

agentRequest.description: POST /agent/v1/browser/request: mark one window (the agent's last one when omitted) as needing the person, or withdraw the request.
